title: Deferred residency handoff and priority throttles for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a controlled "deferred residency handoff" capability to regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets: when a customer's region is under pressure, requests should remain served from the origin region as long as latency and SLA budgets permit. Only when a configurable spill threshold is reached do we perform spillback to a non-resident pool, gated by data residency tags and per-customer consent. Implement priority throttles so high-commitment customers keep their throughput guarantees while lower-tier traffic receives gradual throttling or spill restrictions. This ticket covers policy, runtime routing changes, autoscaler hooks, and operational runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine supports per-customer "defer_until" thresholds (percent of reserved throughput and 95th latency headroom)
Routing layer implements conditional spillback with residency-tag checks and explicit consent flags stored in customer metadata
Autoscaler exposes prewarm (predictive) and reactive modes that interact with defer logic to avoid unnecessary cross-region prewarm
Priority throttle tiering enforces throughput floors for P0/P1 customers with transparent degradation steps for lower tiers
E2E tests simulate region pressure and validate no resident-data leakage and that failover occurs only when configured conditions are met
Observability: dashboard tile showing defer-state, spilled-requests count, per-customer throughput vs reserved, and soft-fail metrics
decisions: Use two-stage spillback: soft-spill (best-effort in-region caching) then hard-spill to non-resident pool once both capacity and latency budgets exhausted
Residency checks operate on request-level metadata; if customer has not opted into cross-region processing, request remains queued or throttled instead of spilling
Autoscaler will expose a 'spill_safety_time' window to avoid oscillation during transient spikes (default 2m)
Implement priority throttles as token-buckets attached to customers with dynamic weights derived from reserved capacity commitments
tasks: Design policy DSL for defer and spill rules — prototype and doc in Confluence
Extend routing layer to evaluate defer rules at request admission and emit metrics
Autoscaler: add hooks to respect defer state and optionally prewarm spill pools when consent present
Implement customer metadata API to store residency consent and throughput commitments
Add unit and integration tests for residency gating, spillback, and throttle enforcement
Create dashboard panels and alert rules for spill events, unusual spill rates, and latency regressions
Draft runbook for on-call: identifying stuck spillbacks, manual override toggle, rollback steps
